reviewed_version.name: ICML 2025 PMLR final PDF
reviewed_version.page_convention: 1-based PDF pages matching printed internal pages

supported_impact: P1 materially affects the quantitative evidence of the stated systematic 115-baseline audit; P2 and P3 remain scoped Minor concerns with the source's precision condition and fairness interpretation retained.

findings.title: Imputed classifications described as observed practices
findings.suspect_step: Defaults for Unknown/Unreported enter statements about what studies reported or displayed.
findings.alternative_reading: The defaults are explicitly disclosed; imputation-dependent assessments are legitimate when labeled as such.
findings.impact: The abstract's stated systematic audit contribution depends on main-text descriptions of recruitment QC and UI/instruction differences. Raw observed categories plus imputed unknowns cannot support the same estimand as explicitly reported/observed practices; three headline rates materially overstate what the annotations establish.

repair.statement: Separate explicit counts, unknowns and assumed classifications.
repair.verification: finite raw-data counts verified; true practices among unknowns unresolved

findings.core_dependency: Abstract and section 1 systematic-audit contribution -> section 4.2/4.3 descriptive practice claims -> Tables 3/6 and codebook defaults -> imputed-versus-observed estimand mismatch.
findings.severity_rationale: Major follows the demonstrated damage to this core quantitative evidence, not the survival of recommendations or difficulty of repair.

findings.title: Survey precision heuristic used to infer statistical power
findings.issue_judgment: supported precision/power conflation; no demonstrated actual-study power failure
findings.check_type: analytic proof with finite numerical verification

counterexample.model: iid Bernoulli(p), known AI probability .5, nominal two-sided alpha .05
counterexample.scope: Illustrates failure of sample-size-only power inference. It does not meet or refute the source's roughly three-percentage-point survey-precision target; it is not a literal counterexample to a stated theorem or an estimate for the reviewed studies.

findings.counterevidence: The source says 'By this standard' and immediately recommends effect-specific power analysis. Its conditional precision interpretation must be preserved.
findings.impact: The sample-size diagnostic requires precision/power clarification; median8 remains verified. No materially false design-specific power conclusion has been demonstrated under matching precision/effect assumptions.

repair.statement: Assess power/precision using relevant effect, variance, design and estimand; use n1000 only as conditional survey illustration.
repair.verification: Conceptual distinction and existing exact illustration checked; no actual-study power recalculation or precision-target falsification claimed.

findings.suspect_step: The source explicitly conditions its phrase 'vastly underpowered' on a survey precision standard. That standard does not identify effect-specific statistical power across heterogeneous baselines.
findings.core_dependency: Section4.1 sample-size diagnostic within the audit. Supported defect is a bounded terminology/transfer issue; the conditional precision reading prevents treating the illustrative high-power design as refutation of the source's exact premise.

findings.title: Prior Internet training equated with live tool access

counterexample.conditions: Independent post-training fair bit posted online; human allowed retrieval; fixed Internet-trained model without retrieval; identical prompt reveals URL not bit
counterexample.scope: Idealized information-access reasoning, not measured behavior

findings.counterevidence: Appendix D proposes that the asymmetric comparison can be fair. The analytic example establishes distinct information access, not unfairness; no universal fairness theorem is asserted.
findings.impact: One construct needs separate operational-access and fairness fields; no source-level recoding or corrected prevalence is claimed.

repair.statement: Record actual tools separately from the fairness rationale; recode affected rows before recomputing.
repair.verification: conceptual distinction verified; dataset-level repair unverified

findings.core_dependency: Appendix B Q3.5 supplies one construct in Table6 and section4.3. Literal tool access is conflated with a fairness proxy; affected explicit rows and a materially false aggregate rate are not established.

scope_clarifications.statement: Same items are practical control; independent representative task samples also permit valid population comparisons.
The maximum target is itemwise; no best-person-average counterexample is asserted.
